run.

Drive the Gattari to critical output. Maximum thrust in minimum time, and then leap—fly—soar. Reckless, one could call it, and I am calling it so myself, but Shinkai's steel held all the same.

The danger of breaking apart in midair I came through, and then I was a single arrow stabbed into the crimson sky.

Speed: touching the six-hundred line. Altitude: a little under nine hundred.◆ Flying any lower than this would be dangerous.

Still accelerating, I brought the flight back to stability.

Yes. Yes, exactly. This is what my death would mean.

My pupils. Raised in purity, beautiful now, at this very moment.

What would become of them?

Sooner or later they would be corrupted. The merciless malice that fills this world would defile them.

I banked into a turn. The enemy shape had taken the high ground again, when I did not even notice, and now it came into my view, and I flew straight at it.

the opponent lowered his head as well and began his descent. A head-on collision, then.

Warrior and warrior. Greatest force against greatest force. The duel that has been repeated in the sky without pause since history began.

And now again, in the sky above Kamakura.

That I would take one side of it myself—yesterday's me, if he heard this, would have laughed it off.

But if it could not be avoided—!

I fixed my eyes firmly on the enemy, still small as a bean.

Hatred went into them. Anger went into them. Fully justified feelings. Not a flicker of hesitation.

No doubt at all. When one appears who obstructs a man doing what must be done, what is there to do but be angry and hate him?

Fear was unnecessary. Conditions were equal.

Then I, who must win, would win!

Muramasa spat out his contempt without a trace of feeling in the voice. I wanted to answer back. Answer I had none.

Aerodynamics I did have, an amateur's trivia, somewhere in memory. When I pulled it out, it confirmed the enemy word for word.

The power of a flying body is positional energy plus kinetic energy. Positional energy is set by weight and height, kinetic energy by weight and speed. Therefore the higher and faster a body flies, the more energy it carries, and so on.

Which means the fool was me, sitting below the enemy and believing we were equal.

Even so, I could not bear the silence. Like a man begging for rescue, I asked Shinkai.

I shook off that irritating voice, which pressed its point as though the speaker were convincing himself. A sermon from a man puffed up on his advantage, lording it over me: such a thing I had no mind to hear.

Reckoning for evil? There is none, just as there is no reward for good. In such a world, only beauty can be trusted. Beauty alone does not betray—except in one point: it is not eternal.

That it must perish, I concede; it cannot be helped. Whatever is done, it cannot be changed. Destiny. I would resign myself and take that curse.

But corruption I could not endure. That the beautiful should turn into something ugly—that alone.

That I would never permit. Never. If I admitted it, beauty would have no value.

How could I admit it?

So I would destroy it. I had to destroy it. The beautiful, while it was still beautiful!

Is that—evil!?
